subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw permit a boolean operator assertion to bypass the WAL-reset guard for any shared SQLite build, or require a verification value tied to the running build or vendor package?
rationale: Either mechanism can be implemented, but deciding how much operator assertion is acceptable for a database-integrity safeguard requires explicit maintainer product and safety policy.

options.title: Require build-bound verification
options.body: Replace the unqualified boolean with a documented value or allowlist tied to the running SQLite build or exact vendor package.

options.title: Accept boolean assertion
options.body: Keep the proposed escape hatch, explicitly own its upgrade risk, and require documentation plus real affected-container proof.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Decline an override and require an upstream-safe SQLite or Node build before startup.

recommendation.title: Require build-bound verification
recommendation.body: Replace the unqualified boolean with a documented value or allowlist tied to the running SQLite build or exact vendor package.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent installer work is the best available ownership signal for OpenClaw's SQLite runtime safety policy.
